# ∫ 3·X²·sin(3·X) dx

Let me work through this indefinite integral step by step.

## Step 1: Set up integration by parts

We want to compute ∫ 3·X²·sin(3·X) dx. I'll use integration by parts.

Let:
- u = 3·X²,  du = 6·X dx
- dv = sin(3·X) dx,  v = -cos(3·X)/3

Then:

∫ 3·X²·sin(3·X) dx = 3·X² · (-cos(3·X)/3) − ∫ (−cos(3·X)/3)·6·X dx

= −X²·cos(3·X) + (1/3)·∫ 6·X·cos(3·X) dx

= −X²·cos(3·X) + 2·∫ X·cos(3·X) dx

## Step 2: Evaluate ∫ X·cos(3·X) dx

Use integration by parts again:
- u = X,  du = dX
- dv = cos(3·X) dx,  v = sin(3·X)/3

∫ X·cos(3·X) dx = X·(sin(3·X)/3) − ∫ (sin(3·X)/3) dx
= (X·sin(3·X))/3 − (−cos(3·X)/3)·(1/3)... 

Actually: ∫ (sin(3·X)/3) dx = (1/3)·∫ sin(3·X) dx = (1/3)·(−cos(3·X)/3) = −cos(3·X)/9

So: ∫ X·cos(3·X) dx = X·sin(3·X)/3 + cos(3·X)/9

## Step 3: Combine

∫ 3·X²·sin(3·X) dx = −X²·cos(3·X) + 2·[X·sin(3·X)/3 + cos(3·X)/9]

= −X²·cos(3·X) + (2/3)·X·sin(3·X) + (2/9)·cos(3·X)

## Step 4: Verify by differentiation

d/dX of [−X²·cos(3X) + (2/3)·X·sin(3X) + (2/9)·cos(3X)]
= −2X·cos(3X) + 3X²·sin(3X) + (2/3)·sin(3X) + 2X·cos(3X) − (2/3)·sin(3X)
= 3·X²·sin(3X) ✓

## Final answer

∫ 3·X²·sin(3·X) dx = −X²·cos(3·X) + (2/3)·X·sin(3·X) + (2/9)·cos(3·X) + C

<answer>
- X**2*cos(3*X) + (2/3)*X*sin(3*X) + (2/9)*cos(3*X) + C
</answer>
